title: News API Guide
heading: Analysis — Market news
intro: Articles from TradingView and FXStreet, each scored for likely market impact and tagged with the instruments it is actually about — so "gold news in the last six hours" is one call, not a search you filter yourself.
Reads never fetch. A background fetcher polls both sources every 30–60 seconds and writes to the database; if a source starts returning nothing, /news/status says which one and how many it brought.

endpoints.title: Get news articles
endpoints.desc: Every filter combines, so you can ask directly: gold news in the last 6 hours, today's high-impact stories, or a topic search.

params.name: symbol
params.desc: Instruments the article is about. Forgiving: gold, XAU/USD, cable, nas100 all resolve.

params.name: impact
params.desc: high | medium | low (comma-separated for several).

params.name: min_score
params.desc: Floor on the 0–100 impact score.

params.name: hours
params.desc: Published in the last N hours (also minutes, days).

params.name: range
params.desc: today | yesterday | this_week | last_7_days.

params.name: since
params.desc: Explicit ISO start on release time (with until).

params.name: until
params.desc: Explicit ISO end.

params.name: source
params.desc: tradingview | fxstreet.

params.name: category
params.desc: Forex Majors, Cryptocurrencies, Commodities, Economic Indicators…

params.name: q
params.desc: Text search over title, description and body.

params.name: full
params.desc: true to include the article body and impact reasons (omitted by default).

params.name: limit
params.desc: Max articles (default 50).

params.name: order
params.desc: desc (newest first, default) or asc.

params.name: pretend_date
params.desc: Answer as if the request were made on this UTC date — e.g. ?pretend_date=2026-08-25&pretend_time=13:12. For backtests and agent reruns that must not see the outcome. Left off, you get the present.

params.name: pretend_time
params.desc: UTC time of day to pair with pretend_date, e.g. 13:12. Omitted, the moment is midnight — not the whole day.

endpoints.title: How heavy the news is
endpoints.desc: Is today busier than yesterday? Counting articles cannot say — ten filler pieces are not louder than one central-bank decision. This returns the SUM of impact scores for a period, with the counts by level and the busiest instruments, and compares it against the window of the same length immediately before, ending with a plain heavier / lighter / similar verdict.

endpoints.title: Fetcher health
endpoints.desc: Last cycle, how many articles are stored, how many arrived last cycle PER SOURCE, and the last error from either. A source that silently returns an empty list is reported as a fault, not as a quiet day.

notes: The impact score is computed from the article, not supplied by the source. Two outlets covering the same release will score alike; a market-moving headline and a colour piece will not.
Instrument tags are earned, not guessed from the title alone — an article about the Fed is tagged for the dollar pairs and the indices it actually moves.

"Is today busier?" is answered by the SUM of impact scores, and the comparison window is the same LENGTH as the one you asked for, ending where it begins. Comparing today against a fixed 24 hours would call every morning quiet.

Any read here accepts pretend_date and pretend_time (UTC) and answers as of that moment: ?pretend_date=2026-08-25&pretend_time=13:12. Anything published later is hidden. Anything merely SCHEDULED for later survives with its actual blanked and pretend_pending set — the schedule was known in advance, the number was not. Responses carry X-Pretend-Time so a replay is never mistaken for the present.
